title: Kianetics: A Specification-Centric Governance Architecture for Runtime Assurance in Agentic AI Systems
content: Agentic artificial-intelligence systems formulate multi-step plans, invoke tools, and mutate operational state. This creates a structural mismatch: action generation is probabilistic, whereas enterprise authorization rules require deterministic enforcement. We present Kianetics, a specification-centric governance architecture reconstituting the security reference monitor for agentic systems. Kianetics separates a terminological layer (T-Box), holding versioned normative constraints, from an assertional layer (A-Box), holding transaction facts. Agent-generated actions are intercepted by a Context Mediation Layer (CML), normalised into canonical intents, and submitted to a deterministic decision service before tool execution. We formalize the architecture as a composition of probabilistic normalisation and deterministic mediation maps, proving decision determinism, risk non-amplification, and error localization within normalisation. Evaluated on two public benchmarks (840 prompt-injection boundary pairs; a 100,000-record PII corpus of which 99,999 records are PII-bearing), mediation reduces attack success from 37.38% to 0.48% (p≈1.7×10-45) on injection and 95.62% to 8.09% (χc2≈8.7×104) on PII, with zero false positives on 420 controls. The decision service exhibits 100% Deterministic Consistency Rate over 500 replays. Latency shows overhead dominated by canonicalisation (median ≈ 1.1 s), with the deterministic service contributing ≈ 20 ms—under 2% of total governance-attributable latency. Results show determinism, auditability and evolvability are obtainable architecturally, without model retraining, and residual attack surface is bounded by normalisation fidelity.
